AddFile.description: **Add as feed**: a file to add to the provider's `files`, with the settings of its feed.

AddUrl.description: Adding a feed by URL (providers.md §3, core.md §12).

provider.description: The id of a provider to create when none fits (default: from the URL).

created_provider.description: A new provider was created for the URL.

existing.description: The URL had its feed already: nothing changed.

feed.description: The feed reading it (an existing one when the URL had a feed already).

file.description: The file added to the provider's `files` (an http provider's one file, `response`).

notice.description: What the UI says about the mapping (jsDelivr's cache).

details.description: Kind-specific detail, rendered as text only (core.md §12).

edge.description:
The edge the alert is about (an edge kind, or a per-edge key such as `wire_mismatch`'s), or
the edge whose log records raised it (a device's or a name's security alert, core.md §9
Grouping). Null when the alert has no edge (a feed, bundle or core alert), or when records
from several edges raised it: those edges are then in `details` where the kind records
them (`details.edges` of `dnssec_bogus` and `upstream_disagrees`).

AlertEvent.description:
An `alert` event's data (api.md §7): alerts raised, repeated, updated, resolved or deleted,
or whose evidence changed, since the previous `alert` event (coalesced: at most one a second, plus one when a restore commits).
Refetch the alert lists (and an alert's evidence that is shown, when `alerts` lists it not
deleted, or is truncated). Changes made before a config restore go out in an event sent
before the `restore` event, never after it.

alerts.description:
Each alert that changed, once, with its state after its latest change, in the order of
their first change; at most 64.

alerts_truncated.description: More alerts changed than `alerts` lists: any alert may have changed.

changes.description:
Changes since the previous event, listed or not, one for each: a raise (new, repeated or
reopened), an update of only an alert's details (more names, edges or clients joining
it), a resolve (also an alert resolved again by hand that already was), a deletion, and
each committed change to an alert's evidence (records copied or counted).

AlertEventItem.description: One alert in an `alert` event (`GET alerts/{id}` has the rest). Every field is always sent.

deleted.description: Deleted: gone with its history and evidence (ids are never reused).

AlertExport.description: One alert: its `alerts` row and its child rows, column by column (BLOBs as `{"b64": …}`).

AlertPage.description: A page of Alert items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

feed_stale_days.description: The days per false `feed_stale` alert its threshold allows (feed-scheduling.md §8).

temporary_allow.description:
Raise `temporary_allow` (security, info) when an edge logs a created temporary allow:
off by default (core.md §9).

thresholds.description:
Alert kind → how long its condition must hold before it fires (core.md §9). Kinds not
listed use core.md §9's defaults: `edge_offline` 5 min; `edge_upstream_down`,
`edge_redirect_missing`, `edge_fw_layout_unknown` and `edge_fw_catch_all` 2 min;
`edge_helper_unreachable` 1 min; `edge_ssd_unavailable` 10 min; `upstream_invalid_spike`
5 min; `feed_down`, `feed_provider_down`, `feed_provider_trigger_down` and
`dnssec_unavailable` 60 min; `lookup_provider_down` 15 min; any other kind at once.

AllowState.description:
A temporary allow's state as core knows it (core.md §12 Temporary allows; storage.md §3
`temp_allows`). Core learns an allow's end from the edge's log; until then an allow whose
revoke the edge acknowledged (`applied.revoked_allows` covered it, api.md §4) is `revoked`:
no longer in force on the edge, though core keeps the row open for the log's end record.

AllowView.description:
One temporary allow on a device (core.md §12 device and profile views): those in force at
some time in the window, newest first.

client.description: The address it was created from.

device.description: The device it is for (its client name or MAC, else null: then `client` names it).

AnswerView.description: The upstream answer a record references, as evidence.

wire.description: The scrubbed answer as logged, base64.

AttributionView.description: A record's attribution as the detail shows it.

decisive.description: The ladder step and bundle replay found decisive.

matches.description: Every match with its feed, text, line, format and role.

unavailable.description: The versions or feed runs that are gone (state `unavailable`).

B64File.description:
A file in base64: a list of chunks (each at most 786432 bytes, 768 KiB, decoded, each
decoding on its own); a restore also reads one string.

B64FileSchema.description: A file in base64 as a restore reads it: a list of chunks, or one string.

oneOf.description: 0.0.0.0 or :: for A/AAAA, NODATA for other types.
`ipv4`/`ipv6` for A/AAAA, NODATA for other types.

enabled.description: Publish this profile's pruned and full browser lists (bundles.md §8).

oneOf.description: Names for lookup scopes; never allows or blocks.
Warninglists; core only.

hot_max_mib.description: Block bundles only: the hot part's cap for `intelligent-tiering` feeds; null = no cap.

system.description: System bundles can be edited but not deleted (read-only).

BundleDefPage.description: A page of BundleDef items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

browser_list.description: The browser list's URL path, when the bundle has one.

building.description: A build is running or waiting.

dry_run.description:
A block bundle's last tiering dry run: how many blocks of the log window would have
come from cold under its proposed split (bundles.md §2 Tiering).

edges.description: The head each edge's current config names for the bundle.

feed_runs.description: The feed runs the last build read, by feed id.

head.description: The head core names (null: no edge bundle, or none yet).

open_alerts.description: Open guardrail and build alerts of the bundle.

shards.description: Per shard: part, shard number, keys, base, chain length, overlay entries, in-memory bytes.

stats.description: The last build's counts and sizes.

rule_types.description: The feed's rule types the bundle takes; null = every type the feed stores.

BundleStatus.description: What the UI shows for one bundle (core.md §12 Bundles).

browser_list.description: The browser list's URL path, when the bundle has one.

building.description: A build is running or waiting.

feed_runs.description: The feed runs the last build read, by feed id.

head.description: The head core names (null: no edge bundle, or none yet).

open_alerts.description: Open guardrail and build alerts of the bundle.

stats.description: The last build's counts and sizes.

BundleVersionEvent.description: A `bundle_version` event's data (api.md §7): a bundle build ended.

head.description: The head it built, null when it built none.

stats.description: The build's statistics (`GET bundles/{id}/versions` keeps them per version).

oneOf.description: Threats.
Ads and tracking.
Both, or not known.

result.description:
`started`, `queued` (a check of the provider is in progress: another runs when it ends)
or `scheduled` (`min_interval`, or the module's rate-limit pause).

version.description: The provider's version at the check.

CheckViewPage.description: A page of CheckView items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

macs.description: `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`; every address an edge sees for them.

position.description: Order in the clients list (lower first); new clients go last when left out.

profile.description: Null: the client only names its devices.

source_ips.description: Address ranges (CIDR or a bare address).

ClientDefPage.description: A page of ClientDef items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

names.description: Every client's name, in the new order.

ConfigChangePage.description: A page of ConfigChange items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

ConfigPreview.description: A preview of an edge's config object as core would render it now (secret values blanked).

id.description: The config's id: BLAKE3 of its bytes.

missing_heads.description: Bundles its profiles reference that have no head yet.

missing_secrets.description: Secrets its sync providers reference that have no value.

secrets.description:
Secrets by name only. On restore a name may carry a `value`; one without keeps the stored
value of that secret.

settings.description: The stored settings rows, by key (a key left out has its default).

Crosscheck.description:
The cross-check of unsigned answers (core.md §8). Off by default: the resolver sees every
name checked.

CrosscheckQueueItem.description:
One queued cross-check of an unsigned answer (core.md §8 Cross-check; the DNSSEC page's
cross-check queue, `GET dnssec/queue`'s `crosscheck_items`, earliest due first). Each (qname,
qtype) is queued once, whichever check flagged it first; later flagged records join it.

attempts.description:
Failed resolver queries so far (timeouts and transport errors); at the third the item ends
as no answer.

kind.description:
The check that queued it: `negative` (an Insecure NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL or A NODATA, after
its DNSSEC result) or `sinkhole` (an allowed answer holding a sinkhole address, flagged at
ingest).

next_at.description:
When it is due: at once when queued, later after a failed query (backoff 30 s to 30 min).
An item queued while core's wall clock wasn't synchronised waits, and its times are set
once the clock is (README §2 Clocks).

qname.description: The name the resolver is asked about.

queued_at.description: When it was queued (or stamped, for an item queued before the clock was synchronised).

operator.description: Who runs the resolver; it must differ from every upstream's operator (core.md §8).

Device.description: One device the edges have seen (core.md §12 Clients).

addresses.description: Addresses it was seen with (most recent first, at most 32).

client.description: The client entry naming the device, if any.

edge.description: The edge that saw it last.

key.description: The device's key in logs: its client name, else its MAC, else its address.

mac.description:
A MAC core currently knows for it: the key itself when it is a MAC; for a device keyed by a
client name, the first MAC of the client entry that has that name now. Null otherwise: for
a client name no entry has now, or whose entry lists no MACs (a MAC logged at its address
before may belong to another device by now), and for an address-keyed device.

macs.description:
The MACs core knows for it (lowercase, at most 16): the key when it is a MAC; for a device
keyed by a client name, the `macs` of the client entry that has that name now (none when
no entry has it or the entry lists none); for an address-keyed device, the MAC most
recently logged as the device of the address it was last seen with, by the edge that saw
it (at most one, and only a hint: that address may be shared or reused, so it is never
the device's `mac`).

name.description: The client entry's name when one names it.

ptr.description: PTR and DHCP host names: core doesn't learn them yet (null).

queries.description: Logged queries in the retention window.

DeviceCount.description: One device in a profile's view.

DnssecEvent.description:
A `dnssec` event's data (api.md §7): DNSSEC validation results stored since the previous
`dnssec` event (coalesced: at most one a second, plus one when a restore commits). Refetch the DNSSEC queue and results.

crosscheck_items.description: The first `limit` of them, earliest due first.

attempts.description: Failed requests so far (an item waiting for a reachable edge uses none).

edges.description: The edges, clients and upstream groups of the records sharing the check.

kind.description:
`answer` (a logged answer), `fallback` (core's own query) or `servfail` (an upstream
SERVFAIL's query, never retried).

received_at.description: The logged answer's `received_at`, the time it is validated as of.

DnssecQueuedEvent.description:
A `dnssec_queued` event's data (api.md §7): the DNSSEC validation and cross-check queues
changed since the previous `dnssec_queued` event (coalesced: at most one a second, plus one when a restore commits). Refetch
the DNSSEC queue (`GET dnssec/queue`). Every change to what it shows sends one, except a
validation result stored, which sends `dnssec` instead (the item leaves the queue then), and
a restore, which sends `restore`.

crosscheck.description: Names queued for the cross-check of unsigned answers (core.md §8 Cross-check).

crosscheck_ended.description: Cross-checks that ended (agree, disagree or no answer) and left the queue.

crosscheck_retried.description: Cross-checks rescheduled after a failed query (core.md §8 Cross-check: 3 attempts).

dropped.description:
Items dropped from either queue: older than the retention window, or queued while the
cross-check is off (core.md §8).

joined.description: Records that joined a queued validation (its records, edges, clients and groups).

retried.description: Validations rescheduled after a failed request (`attempts` moved; core.md §8 backoff).

stamped.description:
Items of either queue given their times once the wall clock was synchronised (README §2
Clocks).

waiting.description:
Validations rescheduled to wait while no edge DoH listener is reachable (core.md §8): each
item's `next_at` moves 30 s on, no attempt used, so each comes again in the queue's order.

answer_id.description: The logged answer and the time it was validated as of (null for core's own query).

groups.description: The upstream groups the records were answered by.

zone.description: The zone where validation broke (Bogus), else null.

listener.description:
The edge DoH listener chains are fetched through; null = the first DoH listener on a
connected edge.

max_per_minute.description: Network requests per minute (chain lookups and fallback queries).

source_ips.description: The addresses edges see core's traffic come from; null = core's own addresses (README §3).

oneOf.description: AdGuard semantics: the name itself.
The name and its subdomains.

blocks.description: Blocks the bundle answered in the window (from any key, pattern or rule).

cold_blocks.description: Of those, blocks from keys the proposed split would place cold.

definition_hash.description: The definition hash the proposed split was taken from.

detail.description: Per proposed tier, the blocks from keys of that tier; the most-blocked cold keys.

proposed.description: `hot_max_mib` and each member feed's tier, as proposed.

started_at.description:
When core first saw the proposal (the split waits for the report until then plus
30 minutes).

EdgeDef.description: A registered edge and its per-edge settings.

bundle_budget_mib.description: Per-edge total of in-memory bundle data in MiB (edge.md §17).

id.description: Stable id (`[a-z0-9-]`); generated when left out.

logging.description: Spool and batch settings; `retention_h` always follows core's `retention.query_logs`.

overlay_budget_mib.description:
Per-edge total of bundle and verdict-set overlays in MiB; null = the platform's default
(16 on UniFi, 4 on Debian).

verdict_budget_mib.description: The UI warns when the edge's sync lookup providers' `max_mib` total passes this.

EdgeStatusEvent.description: An `edge_status` event's data (api.md §7): an edge's session or live state changed.

EdgeStatusView.description: An edge's live state for the UI (`GET /api/ui/v1/edges/{id}/status`).

config.description: The config core serves the edge now.

have.description: What the edge last reported it keeps (api.md §3 `have`).

versions.description: The versions the edge reports active, and those before them.

bundle_budget_mib.description: Per-edge total of in-memory bundle data in MiB (edge.md §17).

id.description: Stable id (`[a-z0-9-]`); generated when left out.

listeners.description: Listener ids assigned to this edge.

logging.description: Spool and batch settings; `retention_h` always follows core's `retention.query_logs`.

overlay_budget_mib.description:
Per-edge total of bundle and verdict-set overlays in MiB; null = the platform's default
(16 on UniFi, 4 on Debian).

verdict_budget_mib.description: The UI warns when the edge's sync lookup providers' `max_mib` total passes this.

EdgeViewPage.description: A page of EdgeView items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

min_firmware.description: Minimum UniFi OS version per target; a release or an admin raises it.

Empty.description: An empty JSON object: every mutating request carries a JSON body (core.md §12).

dropped_at.description: `aggregate` types: when the first applied run without it ran.

raw.description: The rule as written, as first seen (shown as text only).

EntryViewPage.description: A page of EntryView items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

Error.description: The error shape of every UI API error (api.md §2).

issues.description: For a refused save: the problems it would introduce.

EventView.description: One recent edge event or condition change (72 h; core.md §9).

EvidenceLookup.description: One sync lookup's result on an evidence copy, as the edge logged it (api.md §5 `lookups[]`).

cached.description: From the edge's RAM tier or verdict set.

detail.description:
The module's detail: a small JSON object (providers.md §4 "Detail"; ingest refuses
anything else), or null.

gen.description: The provider's `cache_generation` it was obtained under.

obtained_at.description: When the provider answered (a provider's answer only).

EvidenceRecord.description:
One evidence copy (core.md §9 "full copies of its related log records, `response`
included"): the record as the log search shows it, plus what the copy keeps beside it. The
type of `EvidenceView.items`; copies are served as stored (a copy made by an older release
lacks the fields it didn't write).

answer_missing.description: Core never got the referenced answer: only the preview is known.

cold_check.description: Core's check of unchecked cold lookups: `ok`, `missed` or `unavailable`.

cold_unchecked.description: Bundles whose cold check the edge couldn't make.

device.description: The client's name, else the device's MAC, else null.

edns.description: The client's OPT, when it sent one (`{udp, pad}`).

id.description: The record's id in this API (its hour, edge, boot and seq).

incomplete.description: Only the preview is known (`truncated` or `answer_missing`).

lookups.description: Each provider's verdict, reason and detail (api.md §5).

response.description: The reply the edge made (base64), when it logged one.

trial_check.description: When the trial check ran (null before it, or for a record it doesn't check).

wire_check.description: The wire check's result: `ok`, `mismatch`, `skipped`, or null before it ran.

EvidenceRule.description: Which records an alert's evidence copies.

answers.description:
Also records whose answer holds a name under `domain` (its CNAME chain and HTTPS/SVCB
targets, from the referenced answer, else `response`, else the preview): an alert raised
for a target in the answer (`category_answered`, core.md §6 retro-match).

decisions.description: Only records with these decisions (empty: any).

device.description:
Only this device (`category_blocked` keys on (device, domain)): the record's `device`,
else its client address.

domain.description:
Records whose query name is this name or under it (the registrable domain, or the full
name for a name with none).

ips.description: Also records whose answer holds one of these addresses.

profiles.description: Only records of these profiles (empty: any).

answers.description:
The upstream answers this page's copies reference, once each (base64); on the first page
also the answers no copy references (the validator's DNSKEY and DS answers, the
cross-check resolver's).

counts.description:
Exact counts per client and per name; `client_other` and `name_other` hold the rest.
First page only (empty with a `cursor`).

examples.description:
A `wire_mismatch` alert's examples: each record's logged fields, the kind, the answer's
wire (base64: **Download as fuzz case** saves it) and `domain`'s decode or error. First
page only (empty with a `cursor`).

incomplete.description: More than 1,000 distinct clients or names: the breakdown is incomplete.

items.description:
One page of the copied records, newest stored first (by the order core stored them, not
their event times: a backfill or an edge's late spool stores older records later, and
they come first here; the next pages hold the copies stored before): each the whole logged
record, as the log search shows it plus `lookups` (each provider's verdict, reason and detail, api.md §5),
`versions` (the record's version block), `edns` (the client's OPT, when it sent one) and
`response` (base64, when the edge made the reply).

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page: the copies stored before this page's. Null on the
last page. Copies stored while paging come on a fresh first page, never behind a cursor.

rule.description: What capture copies for this alert, if it keeps evidence.

total.description: Copies the alert keeps in all, as this page was read (the same snapshot as its items).

feed_runs.description: The feed runs read (the feeds as they stand now; the published head may be older).

outcome.description:
The reference matcher's outcome (`none`, `block`, `exception`, `allow`, `in_scope`, a
rewrite or host mapping).

alerts.description: Alerts with their history and evidence (each a row of `alerts` and its child rows).

feed_state.description:
Feed check history, learned schedules with their epochs, content hashes and staleness
references (feed-scheduling.md §6, §8).

format_version.description: The document format; this release writes 1 and reads every older one.

manual_files.description: Each manual feed's file, and its latest applied run's blob when that differs.

ExportSize.description: The size of a feed's export and of the file it would make (the UI's warning, feeds.md §4).

body_cap.description: The import body bound the JSON export must fit.

file_bytes.description: Bytes of the file an import of it would make, estimated.

file_cap.description: The download size cap the file must fit.

json_bytes.description: Bytes of the JSON export, estimated.

path.description: Where to download it: `/extension/<file>` (open, no basic auth).

FeedDef.description:
A feed definition (feeds.md §1). Core stores and validates it; checking and ingest are the
feeds module's.

file.description: The provider's file it reads, in the module's terms (read-only); null for a manual feed.

provider.description:
Its feed provider (providers.md §2), set when the provider adds the feed and never
changed (read-only); null for a manual feed.

system.description: System feeds can be edited but not deleted (read-only).

warn_on.description:
Warn bundles to check this feed's entries against where it blocks; null = `["warn-common"]`
for a `security` feed and `[]` otherwise.

FeedDefPage.description: A page of FeedDef items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

FeedExport.description: A feed's JSON export (feeds.md §4): its settings, then each open entry as stored, entries last.

content.description: The file; bytes that aren't UTF-8 read as U+FFFD.

version.description: Pass as base_version when saving an edit of it.

FeedImport.description: A JSON export (first key picket_feed_export, feed before entries), or {"file": "…"} holding a file export or a plain list as text. The body may be gzip-compressed; up to 32 times the download size cap after decompression.

FeedProviderDef.description:
A feed provider (providers.md §2): a configured instance of a download module, which says
where files come from and when to check them. Each file its `files` selects (minus
`exclude`) is one feed.

config.description: The module's settings: what the provider's files share (its `Config` JSON Schema).

exclude.description: Globs of files never to make feeds of (a deleted provider feed's file goes here).

files.description: The files that are its feeds.

system.description: System providers can be edited but not deleted (read-only).

FeedProviderDefPage.description: A page of FeedProviderDef items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

FeedRunEvent.description:
A `feed_run` event's data (api.md §7): feed runs stored since the previous `feed_run` event
(coalesced: at most one a second, plus one when a restore commits). Refetch the feeds' and providers' statuses and runs;
`GET feeds/{id}/runs/{run}` has each run's counts, errors and samples. A run stored before a
config restore is listed in an event sent before the `restore` event, never after it.

runs.description:
The runs stored, in the order they were stored, at most 64: every run of a feed, not only
its latest (a manual feed's editor places each save a run read).

runs_truncated.description:
More runs were stored than `runs` lists: any feed's runs may have changed (an editor
re-reads its feed's runs; a cached manual file is stale).

stored.description: Runs stored since the previous event, listed or not.

FeedRunItem.description:
One stored feed run in a `feed_run` event: what places it (feeds.md §1 manual feeds: the
version and save time it read). Every field is always sent, null where it has no value.

gate.description: The sanity gate that held or rejected it.

saved_at.description: For a manual feed: the save time of the file it read; null for other feeds.

source_run.description: An applied run that reused an earlier run's entries: that run.

busy.description: A check or run is in progress.

file.description: The provider's file it reads (null for a manual feed).

last_change.description: The source's update time of the latest applied run.

manual_retry_at.description:
A manual feed's run that couldn't start (a full heavy lane) or failed: when core tries it
again. With `busy`, it tells "a run is coming" from "no run is coming".

next_check.description: The provider's next check (feeds are checked with their provider).

provider.description: Its feed provider (null for a manual feed).

saved_at.description: When that file was saved: the `updated_at` of the run that reads it (feeds.md §1).

totals.description: Entries per rule type, as the latest run that changed them left them.

version.description:
A manual feed's file version, as `GET feeds/{id}/file` gives it without the content
(null for a provider feed, or before the first save).

FeedStatusPage.description: A page of FeedStatus items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

max_download_mib.description: The download size cap, counted decoded.

max_per_provider.description: The most feeds one feed provider may have (feeds.md §1).

FilePrefix.description: A common prefix of a provider's listing (a folder, with `delimiter=/`).

feeds.description: How many of those a feed reads.

files.description: The files under it, at any depth.

prefix.description: The prefix, ending in `/`: `prefix=` lists it.

FileSave.description: A manual feed's new file. The body may be gzip-compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip).

base_version.description: The version the content was edited from; null only while the feed has no file. Any other: 409.

content.description: The whole file, at most the download size cap (feeds.max_download_mib) decoded.

FileSelect.description:
One entry of a feed provider's `files` (feeds.md §1 "Provider feeds"): a glob for a module
that lists files, a path for one that doesn't, and the settings of the feeds it adds.

feed.description:
Settings of the feeds this entry adds (any feed setting; `format` is required); the
rest take the defaults.

match.description:
A glob (`*` within a path segment, `**` across segments) for a module that lists files,
else a path.

FlushRequest.description: `POST edges/{id}/flush`: flush the DNS cache, or one lookup provider's RAM tier.

provider.description: A lookup provider id: flush its RAM tier on this edge; left out: the DNS cache.

domains_as.description: `plain` format only: how its names match.

fallback.description: `none`: SERVFAIL while the group is down; `default`: fall back to the profile's group.

ForwardZoneDefPage.description: A page of ForwardZoneDef items (cursor pagination).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

HelloInfo.description: What core keeps of an edge's hello (`edge_status.hello_json`).

LancaEvent.description:
A `lanca` UI event's data (api.md §7): the LAN CA's roots changed; refetch `GET settings`.
A `rotated` event goes out before the rotating `PUT settings` is answered, so the tab that
rotated can see it (and its refetch) first.

previous.description:
The previous root: the one the rotation replaced (`rotated`), or the one dropped
(`previous_dropped`, the same as `root`).

root.description:
The root the event is about: the new current root (`rotated`) or the previous root dropped
(`previous_dropped`).

LancaEventKind.description:
What a `lanca` UI event reports (api.md §7; the spec is silent on the event, so it follows the
other events' style).

oneOf.description:
A `lanca.zones` change made `root` the current root and `previous` a previous root, which
stays in use until every listener reports a certificate from the current one (`can_rotate`
false; `lanca_served` events follow the edges' progress).

No listener needs the previous root `root` (= `previous`) any more, so core stopped
trusting it (`can_rotate` true again): the rotation has finished.

LancaServedEvent.description:
A `lanca_served` event's data (api.md §7): while core keeps a previous LAN CA root (a rotation
in progress), edges' reports of the root each managed listener's certificate comes from
changed since the previous `lanca_served` event (coalesced: at most one a second, plus one when a restore commits). Refetch
`GET settings`: `lanca.previous[].edges` loses an edge once all its managed listeners
serve a certificate from the current root, and a `lanca` `previous_dropped` event follows once
none needs the previous root.

edges.description: The edges whose reports changed, at most 64.

zones.description:
The DNS names the LAN CA may sign (core.md §11; default `home.arpa`), first set at `init`.
Changing them rotates the LAN CA to a new root that every device must trust again: a
`PUT settings` with other zones and `lanca.rotate_from` naming the current root
(`lanca.fingerprint`); `lanca.can_rotate` says when one may start.

LancaView.description:
The LAN CA in `GET` and `PUT settings` (core.md §11, §12): its zones and root, and the state of
the last rotation.

can_rotate.description:

synchronised: `clock_synced`).

clock_synced.description:
Whether core's wall clock is synchronised: a rotation is refused (503) until it is (README

download.description: The current root's download path (also on the plain-HTTP port when set).

fingerprint.description:

previous.description:
Previous roots still in use: core keeps trusting them until every assigned managed listener
reports a certificate from the current root, then drops them (a `lanca` `previous_dropped`
UI event; `lanca_served` events tell of the edges' progress meanwhile). Changing
`lanca.zones` is refused (409, code `conflict`) while this isn't empty.

zones.description: `lanca.zones`: the zones the current root signs names under.

RulePolicy.description:
Which rules beyond plain blocks a feed keeps (feeds.md §8). Left-out options take the
default: `drop` for `redirects` and `client_rules`, `keep` for `browser_changes`; manual
feeds keep all three. A dropped rule is dropped whole, never weakened into another.

Each field's description is the UI's tooltip for its drop/keep switch (core.md §12): the
rules it covers with examples, what `keep` lets the feed do, and the default.

browser_changes.description:
Browser changes: `browser` rules that do more than block a request or hide an element:
scriptlets and injections (`example.com##+js(set-constant, x, false)`, `#$#`), action
operators such as `:style()`, modifiers that change a request or response instead of
blocking it (`$redirect`, `$redirect-rule`, `$csp`, `$removeparam`, …) and exceptions
(`@@||example.com^`, `#@#`, `#@?#`, `$badfilter`). `keep` lets the feed run scripts in
pages, change requests and responses, and unblock what other subscribed lists block, in
the browser lists built from it. No effect while the feed's `browser` mode is `drop`.
Default `keep` (browser filter lists rely on scriptlets), for manual feeds too.

client_rules.description:
Client rules: any rule with `$client` or `$ctag` (`||example.com^$client=192.168.1.20`,
`||example.com^$ctag=device_phone`). `keep` lets the feed treat one client differently
from another. Default `drop` (manual feeds: `keep`).

redirects.description:
Redirects: hosts lines that map a name to another IP (`203.0.113.7 example.com`) and
`$dnsrewrite` rules that return records (`||example.com^$dnsrewrite=203.0.113.7`). An
rcode-only `$dnsrewrite` (`NXDOMAIN`, `REFUSED`, an empty `NOERROR`) is a block and
`@@…$dnsrewrite` only cancels; neither counts. `keep` lets the feed answer a name with an
address or record that no upstream sent. Default `drop` (manual feeds: `keep`).
